title: TCS and Rolls-Royce Achieve Breakthrough in Hydrogen-Powered Aviation Test
excerpt: A modified Rolls-Royce Pearl 15 engine ran on 100% hydrogen at full takeoff power at NASA's Stennis Space Center, marking an industry first in the four-year partnership that includes Tata Consultancy Services.
body:
• Rolls-Royce and easyJet successfully tested a modified Pearl 15 aircraft engine running on 100% hydrogen at full takeoff power — an industry first.
  • TCS provided integrated engineering, systems, and software expertise as a key partner in the four-year hydrogen propulsion programme.
  • The engine completed a fully simulated flight cycle including start-up, takeoff, cruise, and landing at NASA's Stennis Space Center in Mississippi.
  • The programme builds on TCS's partnership with Rolls-Royce dating back to 2010, spanning design, manufacturing engineering, and control systems.

Tata Consultancy Services and Rolls-Royce have completed a landmark testing milestone in hydrogen-powered aviation, successfully running a modified aircraft engine on 100% hydrogen at full takeoff power. The test, conducted at NASA's Stennis Space Center in Mississippi, marks the first time a modern aero gas turbine has demonstrated safe hydrogen operation across an entire simulated flight cycle.

What Was Tested

The test involved a modified Rolls-Royce Pearl 15 engine — a powerplant used in business aviation — running entirely on gaseous hydrogen. Engineers demonstrated the engine operating safely through start-up, takeoff, cruise, and landing phases, according to a joint announcement by easyJet and Rolls-Royce.

https://x.com/RIL_Updates/status/2088242035576967674

The programme addressed three core technical challenges: hydrogen fuel combustion, fuel delivery systems, and fuel systems integration with an engine. During development, the team also tested the engine under simulated fault scenarios and at maximum power conditions.

"This programme has given us the clearest understanding in the industry of how hydrogen behaves in a modern aero gas turbine."

— Adam Newman, Chief Engineer, Hydrogen Demonstrator Programme, Rolls-Royce

TCS's Role

TCS served as a key technology partner, providing integrated engineering, systems, and software expertise to accelerate progress across critical workstreams. The Indian IT giant's involvement expanded a partnership with Rolls-Royce that dates back to 2010, covering design, manufacturing engineering, control systems, software, after-market services, and IT.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=V2GIjllJ-CI

Anupam Singhal, President of Manufacturing at TCS, said the milestone "reflects what becomes possible when advanced engineering is combined with digital capabilities and deep ecosystem collaboration to move breakthrough innovation closer to real-world." He added that TCS is "proud to support Rolls-Royce in accelerating hydrogen propulsion" and called the achievement a demonstration of "the industry's readiness to translate ambition into execution."

TCS, part of the Tata Group, reported consolidated revenues of over $30 billion for the fiscal year ending March 2026, with a workforce of 580,000 across 55 countries.

A Four-Year Journey

The hydrogen programme followed an incremental approach. In 2022, easyJet and Rolls-Royce achieved a world first by running a Rolls-Royce AE2100 engine on 100% green hydrogen at Boscombe Down in the UK. In 2023, a full annular combustor from a Pearl engine was tested on 100% hydrogen at the German Aerospace Center (DLR) in Cologne, proving hydrogen combustion at conditions representing maximum takeoff thrust.

The latest test at NASA Stennis brought full integration of the hydrogen system into a demonstrator engine. The UK's Health and Safety Executive developed and tested the pressurised hydrogen infrastructure, while NASA Stennis provided the testing facility and expertise.

What It Means for Aviation

Aviation accounts for roughly 2-3% of global carbon emissions, and the International Air Transport Association has set a target of net-zero carbon emissions by 2050. Hydrogen, which produces no CO2 when burned, is considered one of several pathways to decarbonise the sector alongside sustainable aviation fuels, fleet renewal, and operational efficiencies.

The test results will feed into future Rolls-Royce programmes, including UltraFan, the company's next-generation engine architecture. Adam Newman noted that many insights gained are "fuel agnostic" and applicable beyond hydrogen-specific applications.

David Morgan, Chief Operating Officer at easyJet, called the test "a real testament to the progress our partnership with Rolls-Royce has achieved, taking hydrogen from early concept through to full engine build and successful testing in just a few years."

The Tata Group Connection

TCS's involvement in the hydrogen aviation programme is part of the broader Tata Group's deepening engagement with Rolls-Royce. The partnership encompasses engines and a supply chain commitment that has evolved over more than a decade. For the Indian technology sector, TCS's role in a cutting-edge aerospace programme positions the company — and Indian engineering — at the frontier of the global energy transition in aviation.
